authoringStatement: M0 expectations were authored by hand before any production SMF parser, sonority grouper, or reverse resolver existed. Every hostile and well-formed byte fixture was assembled from the SMF 1.0 byte model (chunk layouts, VLQ arithmetic, running status, meta payloads); repeated limit segments were produced by the authoring session's own byte arithmetic, never by any production code. Every window, grid, measure, counter, offset, and alternative-set expectation was derived on paper with the exact integer formulas frozen in the manifest and cross-checked against the validator's independent reference implementations. The round-trip golden restates the E1-GLD-001 writer fixture byte-for-byte and pins it; no value was produced by, or copied from, production output.

classificationPolicy.primary-standard: A current normative specification of an external format or Web platform capability.
classificationPolicy.reviewed-contract: A normative repository architecture or package decision.
classificationPolicy.legacy-observation: A reproduced legacy failure the replacement must not preserve.
classificationPolicy.mechanical-derivation: A direct result of a declared formula, integer algorithm, or cap.
classificationPolicy.human-review: A judgment that automation cannot honestly certify.

authorities.source: Standard MIDI File 1.0 specification (MMA): header/track chunk layout, big-endian integers, variable-length quantities of at most four bytes, running status with meta/sysex cancellation, velocity-zero note-off equivalence, meta event types and payload layouts, format 0/1/2 semantics, PPQ versus SMPTE division, alien-chunk tolerance, and the 120 bpm / 4-4 defaults
supports: The accepted-format and division envelope and every smf.* refusal class
Running status across meta cancellation and multi-channel status changes
Velocity-zero note-offs and note pairing per (track, channel, key)
Tolerated meta and channel-message vocabularies recorded, never silent
Default tempo 500000 and default meter 4/4 as recorded laws

authorities.source: docs/T1_RESOLUTION_CONTRACT.md and src/theory/resolution-contract.ts: the frozen CHORD_FORMULA_RULE_IDS vocabulary, the four altered-dominant realization ids and their degree sets, and the Custom-chord limitation law
supports: Every template's formulaRuleId is an existing T1 rule id; none is invented
The four alt templates restate the T1 ALT_VARIANT degree sets as pitch-class offsets
The no-confident-symbol outcome is the T1 Custom shape: literal pitches, no analysis claim
Symbol text rendering is deferred to the T0 formatter so the grammar cannot fork

authorities.source: docs/E1_MIDI_EXPORT_CONTRACT.md, src/export/midi-export-contract.ts, and tests/fixtures/midi-export/golden-cases.json: the writer's frozen meta vocabulary, PPQ-960 plan pins, and the byte-golden corpus
supports: The consumed meta vocabulary is byte-identical to MIDI_EXPORT_META_TYPES
M0-GLD-001 restates E1-GLD-001 byte-for-byte and the validator pins the equality
The 4 MiB byte cap mirrors MAX_MIDI_EXPORT_BYTES and the note cap mirrors the writer's
Import-only golden families are exactly shapes the E1 writer can never emit

authorities.source: Integer and exact-rational arithmetic over frozen values: floor(40000*ppq/microseconds) windows, the floor((2N+D)/(2D)) grid law, ceil segment-measure counts, VLQ and chunk-length sums, refusal byte offsets, limit thresholds, and deterministic work/state/memory counters
supports: Every windowTicks, gridIndex, quantized rational, error rational, and measureIndex
Every refusal byteOffset under the manifest offsetSemantics
Every expectedCounters record and every limit-case threshold offset
The ranking tuples behind every alternative ordering

authorities.source: M0/spec authoring session for jcpe-v3c2.1: fixtures hand-assembled and cross-checked against the validator's independently written reference decoder, grouper, and matcher
supports: Expectations authored before production and never regenerated from it
The 40 ms window constant chosen inside the owner's 30-60 ms band and frozen as musical time, not wall time

The flat-preferring canonical import spelling table
